schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

customManagers.description: The docpress release the action runs by default, marked with a 'renovate:' comment above the default of the version input

packageRules.description: Group non-major updates into a single PR to keep review cheap
Majors stay separate, they need a deliberate look

Actions embedded in action.yml run on behalf of consumers, so bumps land as 'fix' to cut a patch release and move the v0 tag downstream repos consume. Our release-please config (release-type: simple, default versioning strategy) only bumps the version for 'fix'/'feat'/breaking commits, not 'build' or 'chore' - so this must stay 'fix' to actually trigger a release. They get a group of their own, so that the chores of the non-major group do not decide the type of their commit.
docpress is ours: a release reaches the action at once, in a PR of its own, as 'fix' for release-please to cut a release of the action and move the v0 tag
Actions used only by this repo's own CI/CD workflows don't affect consumers, so keep them as chores - no need to cut a release for internal tooling bumps.
Keep the bun pin in package.json and mise.toml in one PR
No wait for our own reusable workflows: a fix released there has to reach this repository at once

Lock file maintenance has no release timestamp for Renovate to age, so with minimumReleaseAge set its renovate/stability-days status stays pending forever. bun enforces the same age itself while it regenerates bun.lock (bunfig.toml), which is the check that actually protects the lock file
